title: Applied anatomy: knee ligaments and menisci

guidelineVersions: Benjaminse et al., J Orthop Sports Phys Ther (2006)
Shelbourne and Nitz, Am J Sports Med (1991)

related.why: Knee examination: performing the tests whose anatomy is covered here
Popliteal fossa and common peroneal nerve at the back of the same joint

brief.scenario: Gregor Munro, 26, twisted his right knee playing football with his foot planted. He felt a pop, the knee swelled within two hours, and it now gives way. The examiner will ask you about the anatomy of the knee ligaments and menisci, and will read out any examination and MRI findings you ask for.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the knee ligaments and menisci and relate them to his injury.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Each structure: attachments, what it resists, how it is injured, which test stresses it.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Reciting examination steps instead of explaining the anatomy behind them.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The cruciates are named by where they attach on the tibia."

grid.label: Joint
grid.pass: Modified hinge synovial joint: femoral condyles on the tibial plateau, plus the patellofemoral joint. Stability depends on ligaments and muscles, not bony shape.
grid.high: Adds rotation: the femur rotates medially on the tibia in full extension to lock, and popliteus unlocks it.

grid.label: Cruciate ligaments
grid.fail: Swaps what the ACL and PCL resist.
grid.pass: ACL: anterior tibia to the lateral femoral condyle; resists anterior tibial translation. PCL: posterior tibia to the medial femoral condyle; resists posterior translation.
grid.high: Adds that the ACL also resists rotation, which the pivot shift tests; they are intracapsular but extrasynovial.

grid.label: Collateral ligaments
grid.fail: Cannot say which stress each resists.
grid.pass: MCL: medial epicondyle to medial tibia; resists valgus. LCL: lateral epicondyle to fibular head; resists varus.
grid.high: MCL deep fibres attach to the medial meniscus; the LCL is separate from the lateral meniscus, with popliteus tendon between.

grid.label: Menisci
grid.fail: Cannot describe their shape or role.
grid.pass: Fibrocartilage; medial C-shaped, lateral more circular. They spread load, deepen the plateau and aid stability. Medial is less mobile, so tears more.
grid.high: Only the peripheral rim is vascular, so peripheral tears may be repaired; a displaced bucket-handle tear locks the knee.

grid.label: Test to structure
grid.fail: Cannot link a test to the structure it stresses.
grid.pass: Lachman and anterior drawer: ACL. Posterior drawer and sag: PCL. Valgus and varus stress in slight flexion: MCL and LCL. McMurray, Thessaly: menisci.
grid.high: Lachman is the most accurate ACL test: sensitivity 85%, specificity 94%; pivot shift is highly specific, 98%.

grid.label: Relating to his injury
grid.fail: Suggests a simple sprain despite rapid swelling.
grid.pass: Pop, swelling within hours and giving way suggest haemarthrosis from an ACL tear. MRI to confirm and look for associated injuries.
grid.high: Knows the classic triad (ACL, MCL, medial meniscus) and that the lateral meniscus is more often torn with combined ACL and MCL injury.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What kind of joint is the knee?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It stops the tibia moving backwards.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: They support the sides of the knee.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you test the ACL?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Probably a sprain. Rest and review.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A modified hinge synovial joint: the femoral condyles on the tibial plateau, plus the patellofemoral joint. It relies on ligaments and muscles for stability.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: They're named by their tibial attachment. The ACL runs from the anterior tibia to the lateral femoral condyle and stops the tibia sliding forwards. The PCL runs from the posterior tibia to the medial femoral condyle and stops it sliding back.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The MCL runs from the medial epicondyle to the tibia and resists valgus. The LCL runs to the fibular head and resists varus.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Fibrocartilage wedges: the medial is C-shaped, the lateral more circular. They spread load and deepen the plateau. The medial is less mobile, so it tears more.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Lachman and anterior drawer for the ACL, posterior drawer for the PCL, valgus and varus stress at 30 degrees for the collaterals, McMurray for the menisci.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A pop, swelling within hours and giving way suggest a haemarthrosis from an ACL tear. I'd request an MRI.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In full extension the femur rotates medially on the tibia and locks. Popliteus unlocks it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It also controls rotation, which is what the pivot shift reproduces. Both cruciates are inside the capsule but outside the synovium.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why does the medial meniscus tear more?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The deep MCL fibres attach to it, so it's tethered. The LCL is separate from the lateral meniscus, with popliteus tendon between.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Only the peripheral rim has a blood supply, so peripheral tears can be repaired. A bucket-handle tear can flip into the notch and lock the knee.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Lachman: in a meta-analysis sensitivity was 85% and specificity 94%. The pivot shift is 98% specific but insensitive.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: O'Donoghue's triad: ACL, MCL and medial meniscus. In athletes with ACL and MCL tears, the lateral meniscus is actually torn more often, so the MRI should look at both.

failures.move: Saying the ACL resists posterior translation.
failures.consequence: Cannot interpret the drawer tests or the MRI.

failures.move: Calling rapid swelling after a pop a sprain.
failures.consequence: Misses an ACL tear and associated meniscal injury.

failures.move: Using a meniscal test to assess the ACL.
failures.consequence: Shows the test is not linked to the anatomy it stresses.

recovery.line: Named by the tibia: anterior cruciate starts at the front of the tibia.
A displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear until proven otherwise.

knowledge.fact: ACL: anterior intercondylar tibia to lateral femoral condyle. PCL: posterior intercondylar tibia to medial femoral condyle.
MCL deep fibres attach to the medial meniscus; the LCL does not attach to the lateral meniscus.
Lachman test: pooled sensitivity 85%, specificity 94% for ACL rupture.
Combined ACL and MCL tears in athletes: lateral meniscal tears outnumber medial.

recall.think: Pop plus rapid swelling means haemarthrosis: ACL until proven otherwise.
recall.say: "Cruciates are named by their tibial attachment."
do: Map each structure to the stress it resists
Link each test to that stress
MRI for ACL and both menisci

numbers.meaning: Lachman sensitivity / specificity for ACL rupture

recall.trap: The 'unhappy triad' is classic, but the lateral meniscus is often the one torn.
recall.finish: MRI; reconstruction discussed for young active patients with instability.

partner.opening: Describe the knee joint, then each ligament that crosses it: where it attaches and what it resists.

reveals.finding: Read out: viewed from above, the tibial plateau carries two crescent-shaped fibrocartilage wedges, one on each condyle. Two ligaments arise from the non-articular area between the condyles, one at the front and one at the back.
Read out: tense effusion within two hours of injury.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the Lachman result
reveals.finding: Read out: increased anterior translation with a soft end point.
Read out: the MRI report shows a complete ACL tear, a grade 2 MCL sprain and a tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.

push.question: What do the cruciates resist?
push.expect: ACL anterior translation and rotation; PCL posterior translation.

push.question: Why does the medial meniscus tear more easily?
push.expect: Tethered to the deep MCL, less mobile.

push.question: Which part of a meniscus can heal?
Which ACL test is most accurate?
What is the unhappy triad?
push.expect: ACL, MCL, medial meniscus; lateral meniscus is often torn instead.

curveballs.prompt: He comes back unable to straighten the knee fully.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Locked knee: displaced bucket-handle meniscal tear; urgent MRI and arthroscopy.

curveballs.prompt: Why test the MCL at 30 degrees?
curveballs.safeAnswer: At full extension the cruciates and capsule also resist valgus; flexion isolates the MCL.

curveballs.prompt: Why is the ACL called anterior?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Named by its tibial attachment on the anterior intercondylar area.
